title: Minerva Humanoids raises $10M for robots that do bomb disposal and rig work
key_facts: Minerva Humanoids, San Francisco, raised about $10M pre-seed; General Catalyst led, with Long Journey Ventures and Credo Ventures as co-leads.
Hugging Face, Codecademy, RunwayVC and Compound also back it.
First paid pilots start this autumn.
Its robot Roger is semi-autonomous: a trained specialist operates it via VR headset for fine work, while its AI handles balance, fall recovery and navigation.
Targets: offshore oil rigs, high-voltage power plants, explosive ordnance disposal and hazardous-material response; exploring two of the world’s ten busiest airports.
Company estimates about 7,000 energy workers die on the job yearly, applying an ILO rate to 76 million IEA-counted workers.
First prototypes built in Germany; plans to avoid single-source Chinese components.
quote_evidence: The company estimates that about 7,000 energy workers die on the job every year.
why_it_matters_hint: Funding for a humanoid robot meant to take people out of the most dangerous jobs.
notes: Company statements relayed by The Next Web; the death estimate is the company’s own calculation.
